claims.text: The Transformer is a new simple network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
Transformer models are superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train compared to recurrent and convolutional approaches.
The Transformer achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over existing best results including ensembles by over 2 BLEU.
The Transformer establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 on WMT 2014 English-to-French after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs.
The Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.
The Transformer generalizes well to other tasks such as English constituency parsing.

mechanism.title: Input embedding
mechanism.detail: Convert input tokens to vectors using learned embeddings of dimension d_model. Multiply embedding weights by sqrt(d_model).

mechanism.title: Positional encoding
mechanism.detail: Add positional encodings to input embeddings at the bottoms of encoder and decoder stacks. Use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: PE(pos,2i) = sin(pos/10000^(2i/d_model)) and PE(pos,2i+1) = cos(pos/10000^(2i/d_model)).

mechanism.title: Encoder stack
mechanism.detail: Stack of N=6 identical layers. Each layer has two sub-layers: (1) multi-head self-attention mechanism, (2) position-wise fully connected feed-forward network. Residual connection around each sub-layer followed by layer normalization: LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)). All sub-layers produce outputs of dimension d_model=512.

mechanism.title: Multi-head self-attention in encoder
mechanism.detail: Linearly project queries, keys, values h=8 times with different learned projections to d_k, d_k, d_v dimensions respectively. Perform attention function on each projected version in parallel, yielding d_v-dimensional outputs. Concatenate and project to final values. In practice: h=8 heads, d_k=d_v=d_model/h=64.

mechanism.title: Feed-forward network in encoder
mechanism.detail: Position-wise fully connected feed-forward network applied to each position separately: FFN(x) = max(0, xW_1 + b_1)W_2 + b_2. Linear transformation with ReLU activation followed by another linear transformation. Input/output dimension d_model=512, inner-layer dimension d_ff=2048.

mechanism.title: Decoder stack
mechanism.detail: Stack of N=6 identical layers. Each layer has three sub-layers: (1) multi-head self-attention with masking to prevent attending to subsequent positions, (2) multi-head encoder-decoder attention over encoder stack output, (3) position-wise feed-forward network. Residual connections and layer normalization around each sub-layer.

mechanism.title: Masked self-attention in decoder
mechanism.detail: Self-attention layer preventing positions from attending to subsequent positions by masking out (setting to -infinity) all softmax input values corresponding to illegal connections. Ensures predictions for position i depend only on known outputs at positions less than i.

mechanism.title: Encoder-decoder attention
mechanism.detail: Queries come from previous decoder layer, memory keys and values come from encoder output. Allows every position in decoder to attend over all positions in input sequence.

mechanism.title: Output projection and softmax
mechanism.detail: Linear transformation converts decoder output to predicted next-token probabilities. Share same weight matrix between two embedding layers and pre-softmax linear transformation.

concepts.name: Attention function
concepts.definition: Maps a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output, computed as a weighted sum of values where weights are determined by a compatibility function of the query with corresponding keys.

concepts.name: Scaled dot-product attention
concepts.definition: Computes attention by taking dot products of queries with keys, dividing each by sqrt(d_k), and applying softmax to obtain weights on values.

concepts.name: Multi-head attention
concepts.definition: Instead of single attention function, linearly project queries, keys, values h times with different learned projections, perform attention in parallel on each, concatenate and project results. Allows model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces.

concepts.name: Self-attention
concepts.definition: An attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence. All keys, values, and queries come from the same place (previous layer output).

concepts.name: Positional encoding
concepts.definition: Information about relative or absolute position of tokens in sequence added to input embeddings. Uses sinusoidal functions of different frequencies to allow model to learn to attend by relative positions.

concepts.name: Encoder-decoder attention
concepts.definition: Multi-head attention where queries come from decoder layer and keys/values come from encoder output, allowing decoder to attend over input sequence.

concepts.name: Residual connection
concepts.definition: Feedforward connection around sub-layers such that output = LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)), used to facilitate training.

concepts.name: Layer normalization
concepts.definition: Normalization technique applied after residual connections in each sub-layer, following form: LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)).

concepts.name: Dot-product attention
concepts.definition: Attention mechanism identical to scaled dot-product attention. Faster and more space-efficient than additive attention as it can be implemented using optimized matrix multiplication.

comparisons.text: Self-attention layers connect all positions with constant O(1) sequential operations, whereas recurrent layers require O(n) sequential operations. Self-attention is faster than recurrent when sequence length n is smaller than representation dimension d.

Single convolutional layer with kernel width k<n does not connect all pairs of positions, requiring O(n/k) convolutional layers for contiguous kernels or O(log_k(n)) for dilated convolutions to connect all pairs, increasing maximum path length. Convolutional layers are more expensive by factor of k.

Self-attention complexity per layer is O(n^2·d) with O(1) maximum path length. Recurrent complexity is O(n·d^2) with O(n) maximum path length. Convolutional complexity is O(k·n·d^2) with O(log_k(n)) maximum path length.

comparisons.text: Transformer (big) achieves 28.4 BLEU on EN-DE vs 26.36 BLEU for ConvS2S Ensemble and 26.30 BLEU for GNMT+RL Ensemble, at a fraction of training cost (2.3×10^19 FLOPs vs 7.7×10^19 to 1.8×10^20 FLOPs).
Transformer (big) achieves 41.8 BLEU on EN-FR, outperforming all previous single models like ConvS2S Ensemble (41.29 BLEU), at less than 1/4 the training cost of previous state-of-the-art.

Dot-product attention is identical to additive attention except for scaling factor of 1/sqrt(d_k). Dot-product is much faster and more space-efficient in practice as it can be implemented using optimized matrix multiplication code.

whys.text: Recurrent models have sequential computation that precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longer sequence lengths as memory constraints limit batching. The Transformer uses attention to allow parallelization.

Dot products grow large in magnitude for large d_k, pushing softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. Scaling dot products by 1/sqrt(d_k) counteracts this effect. This is because when components of q and k are independent random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, their dot product has variance d_k.
Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. With single attention head, averaging inhibits this.

Sinusoidal positional encoding was chosen because it allows the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset k, PE(pos+k) can be represented as a linear function of PE(pos). Also allows extrapolation to sequence lengths longer than training.

Three desiderata motivated use of self-attention: (1) total computational complexity per layer, (2) amount of parallelizable computation (minimum sequential operations), (3) path length between long-range dependencies (shorter paths make learning dependencies easier).
Self-attention layers are used instead of sequence-aligned recurrence to enable full parallelization and reduce maximum path length to constant operations.

The Transformer uses multi-headed attention with reduced dimensions per head (d_k = d_v = 64 for 8 heads) because the total computational cost remains similar to single-head attention with full dimensionality.
Residual connections and layer normalization facilitate the training of deep networks by allowing gradient flow and stabilizing activations.
Dropout is applied to prevent over-fitting during training and is helpful as evidenced by ablation studies in Table 3 rows (D).
Label smoothing (epsilon_ls=0.1) hurts perplexity but improves accuracy and BLEU score by making the model learn to be more unsure.
Sinusoidal positional encoding was chosen over learned embeddings because experiments showed nearly identical results but sinusoidal version allows extrapolation to longer sequences.

limits.text: For tasks with very long sequences, self-attention could be restricted to considering only a neighborhood of size r around the output position, increasing maximum path length to O(n/r). This approach requires further investigation.
Future work plans to apply attention-based models to other tasks and extend Transformer to problems with input/output modalities other than text.
Plans to investigate local, restricted attention mechanisms to efficiently handle large inputs and outputs such as images, audio and video.
Making generation less sequential is another research goal.
